 PAPER 2 (313/2)
10 Sample Papers + Answers
SAMPLE PAPER 1
313/2
CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION PAPER 2
1. (a) With reference to St. Luke’s Gospel state the mission of John the Baptist as prophesied by his
 father in the Benedictus 4mks)
 (b) Give the teachings of John the Baptist about the Messiah (8mks)
 (c) How do Christians today play the role of John the Baptist? (8mks)
2. (a) Describe the reasons why Jesus taught in parables (6mks)
 (b) Explain the qualities of God from the parable of the prodigal son (8mks)
 (c) Identify ways in which the disciples of Jesus reacted to his parables (6mks)
3. (a) Explain the role of the Holy Spirit as taught by Jesus Christ (8mks)
 (b) Relate the message of Peter on the day of Pentecost (7mks)
 (c) How are the gifts of the Holy Spirit manifested in the church today? (5mks)
4. (a) State the factors that lead to sexual immorality among the youth today (8mks)
 (b) Give guidelines that can help boys and girls to lead responsible sexual lives (6mks)
 (c) Describe the social and the moral effects of HIV/AIDS on the family (6mks)
5. (a) Give the qualities a Christian would look for in a prospective marriage partner (7mks)
 (b) Give the characteristics of responsible parenthood (8mks)
 (c) Family life today is faced with innumerable problems. List some of them (5mks)
6. (a) Give reasons why people work (6mks)
 (b) Explain some of the factors that bring about unemployment in Kenya today (8mks)
 (c) What are the negative results brought about by a strike action in a school situation?
 (6mks)

SAMPLE PAPER 1
313/2
1. a) With reference to St. Luke’s Gospel state the Mission of John the Baptist as prophesied
 by his
 father in the Benedictus (4mks)
 i) He would be the prophet of the most high
 ii) He would go before the Lord to prepare the road for him/ he would be the
 forerunner of the Messiah
 iii) His duty would involve imparting the knowledge of salvation to the people
 iv) He would call people to repentance and forgiveness in order to restore the right
 relationship with God
 v) He would give ‘light’ to those living in darkness and guide them into path of
 peace
 Any 4x1=4
 mks
 b) Give the teachings of John the Baptist about the Messiah (8mks)
 i) He was going to be famous and greater than John the Baptist
 ii) He would baptise with the Holy Spirit and fire
 iii) He would bring God’s salvation/ saviour/ save humanity
 iv) He will proclaim judgement
 v) He will punish the sinners and reward the righteous/ give eternal life
 vi) Jesus is the Messiah/ Christ is the anointed one
 vii) Jesus as the lamb who takes away the sins of the world/ Christ would die for the
 sins of humanity
 viii) Jesus will be a Lord and a judge
 ix) Jesus will lead the new community of believers
 x) Christ was sent by God/ He is from God Any 8x1=8
 mks
 c) How do Christians today play the role of John the Baptist? (8mks)
 i) John baptised the believers; Christians today baptise those who believe
 ii) John preached and called people to repentance; Christians today preach and call
 people to repentance
 iii) Like John Christians should announce the consequences of not believing in
 Christ’s salvation
 iv) Like John Christians should be bold enough to condemn evil in society
 v) Like John advised the tax collectors to be honest, Christians should advice people
 to be honest and not practice corruption
 vi) John proclaimed Christ as the lamb of God who takes away the sins of the world,
 Christians should do the same today
 vii) John taught against accusing people falsely, Christians should preach and practice
 justice
 viii) John taught on sharing, therefore Christians should not only preach but also
 practice it
 ix) Christians should realise that Christianity alone without sincerity cannot justify
 their entry into the kingdom of God Any 8x1=8 mks
2. a) Describe the reasons why Jesus taught in parables (6mks)
 i) To distinguish the serious seekers of the kingdom from those who were just eager
 listen to the story
 ii) To explain unknown issues in a language people could easily understand
 iii) To make people think critically about issues concerning the Kingdom
 iv) They were used by Jesus to teach about God’s Kingdom
 v) To teach about God’s mercy to sinners i.e. parable of the debtors/ parable of lost
 coin
 vi) To conceal his true identity as the Messiah
 vii) To teach about the requirement of God’s Kingdom
 viii) Parables were avenues of passing important teachings to the people, how to relate
 to one another, how to use wealth and even how to pray
 ix) It was a method of teaching which was common those days
 x) To teach his disciples that they should be persistent and never be discouraged
 (Lk18:1-8)
 xi) He wanted to make an indirect attack on his opponents like the Pharisees, the
 scribes and the Sadducees
 Any 6x1=6 mks
b) Explain the qualities of God from the parable of the prodigal son (8mks)
 i) God is a God of freedom who has given man freedom to choose as the father
granted the
 wishes of the younger son
 ii) God responds to people’s prayer and request as the father listened to the wishes of
 his younger son
 iii) God is always concerned about sinners as the father was looking forward to the
 return of his son
 iv) God is merciful and compassionate and ready to receive those who repent as the
 father welcomed his son
 v) God is a loving father as he loves us unlimitedly the way the father loved his
 younger son
 vi) God is happy and rejoices when the repentant sinner go back to him i.e. when the
 lost one is found as the father rejoiced when the son came back
 vii) God is forgiving as the father forgave his son
 viii) God does not discriminate against some people. All people are his children just
 like the father did not discriminate against his son
 ix) God is generous as shown by the father who gave his younger son part of his
 property and told the older one that all my wealth is yours
 x) God is mysterious i.e. the older son could not understand what the father was
 doing
 xi) God provides as he is the provider and giver; this is seen in the father giving his
 younger son a ring and clothing
 xii) God knows and understands each individual needs as the father knew the needs of
 his sons Any
 8x1=8 mks
 c) Identify ways in which the disciples of Jesus reacted to his parables (6mks)
 i) They were surprised at the meaning and reasons for the use of parables
 ii) They failed to understand the message of some of the parables
 iii) They asked Jesus to explain the parables
 iv) They felt privileged
 v) They understood some parables clearly
 vi) They marvelled at Jesus ability to teach using parables
 vii) They enjoyed listening to Jesus parables
 viii) They felt challenged by Jesus parables
3. a) Explain the role of the Holy Spirit as taught by Jesus Christ (8mks)
 i) He would be a counsellor/ advocate/ a comforter / aiding believers / helpers
 ii) He would convict people about sins, righteousness and the coming judgement
 iii) He would remind the believers everything that Jesus had taught them
 iv) He would reveal the truth concerning God the father and Jesus the son
 v) He would pass judgement to the sinners
 vi) He would declare things to come through the believers
 vii) He will glorify Jesus by declaring what belongs to Jesus Christ from the father
 viii) He would teach the believers of all things and reveal the sins of the world
 ix) He would give authority to the believers to forgive sin
 x) He would give the believers power to become witnesses of Jesus Christ
 xi) He would enable the believers to discern and expose the secret heart of sinful
 people
 xii) He would affirm the right of Jesus as the son of God Any 8x1=8 mks
 b) Relate the message of peter on the day of Pentecost (7mks)
 i) What was happening was the fulfillment of Joel’s prophecy about the outpouring
 God’s spirit
 ii) The outpouring of the Holy Spirit was a positive proof that the Messianic age had
 arrived through Jesus Christ
 iii) Jesus was from Nazareth through whom God worked miracles
 iv) Jesus suffered and was crucified by sinful people in accordance with God’s plan
 v) God raised Jesus up to fulfill the prophecy of King David
 vi) The apostles are living witnesses to the resurrection of Jesus
 vii) God has exalted Jesus and made him both God and saviour
 viii) Jesus is a descendant of David
 ix) Peter told the people to repent so that they could be forgiven and receive the gift
 of the Holy Spirit Any 8x1=8
 mks
 c) How are the gifts of the Holy Spirit manifested in the Church today? (5mks)
 i) People speaking in tongues
 ii) People healing the sick
 iii) Performing miracles e.g. casting out demons
 iv) Proper understanding and interpretation of God’s message
 v) Proper/ wise decision making and right believing
 vi) Giving of prophetic messages to the church
 vii) Ability to withstand challenges of life/ persecution
 viii) Helps believers to repent and seek forgiveness for their sins
 ix) The believers loving one another
 x) Charity work done by believers Any 5x1=5
 mks
4. a) State the factors that lead to sexual immorality among the youth today
 i) Human weakness
 ii) Sexual curiosity
 iii) Testing fertility
 iv) Fear of being jilted by boy/ girl friend
 v) Poverty
 vi) Availability of contraceptives
 vii) Negative peer pressure and bad company
 viii) Influence from print and electronic media
 ix) Frustrations
 x) Unemployment
 xi) Drug and alcohol abuse
 xii) Proving manhood Any 8x1=8 mks
b) Give guidelines that can help boys and girl to lead responsible sexual lives (6mks)
 i) Avoid physical contact like kissing and hugging
 ii) Avoid conversations on topics that are sexually suggestive
 iii) Dwell on positive thoughts about your special friend as a way of controlling your
 desires
 iv) Avoid meeting in lonely and isolated places
 v) Avoid social functions such as discos and parties that may create room for sexual
 abuse
 vi) Avoid visiting each other frequently
 vii) Avoid pornographic literature, films and music
 viii) Seek guidance from Christian leaders and counselors on your relationship
 ix) Study the Bible teachings on sex
 x) Pray for God’s guidance Any 6x1=6 mks
c) Describe the Social and Moral effects of HIV/AIDS on the family
 i) Economic contribution of the AIDS patient is drastically reduced
 ii) It increases the medical expenses as the person is often sick
 iii) The AIDS patient eventually dies and this brings sorrow to the family
 iv) Emergence of children- headed households
 v) Dropping out of school by the children
 vi) Discrimination against people living with AIDS in work place, and may not be
 hired for jobs
 vii) Stigmatisation of AIDS sufferers
 viii) Feeling of loneliness, isolation and helplessness
 ix) Grandparents are burdened with taking care of orphans
 x) Work load for women in the family set-up increases because they have to provide
 for the family Any
 6x1=6 mks
5. a) Give the qualities a Christian would look for in a prospective marriage partner (7mks)
 i) Commitment to ones faith
 ii) Moral uprightness
 iii) Common interest
 iv) Ability to provide for the family
 v) Socio- economic status
 vi) Level of education
 vii) Common faith
 viii) Good management of family finances
 ix) Health status Any 7x1=7
 mks
 b) Give the characteristics of responsible parenthood (8mks)
 i) Understanding parental roles and responsibilities
 ii) Educating children in all aspects of life
 iii) Teaching and training children in religious matters
 iv) Helping their children to grow physically, socially, psychologically and
 emotionally
 v) Helping children to develop intellectually by providing opportunities for them to
 learn
 vi) Teaching morals and right behaviour to their children
 vii) Teaching children on how to relate with another as brothers and sisters, among
 other relatives and kinsmen and among their peers
 viii) Teaching them social and civic responsibilities
 ix) Being hardworking so that they are able to provide for the needs of their families
 x) Parents should remember not to discriminate against any of their children
 xi) Showing understanding and tolerance to their children Any 8x1=8
 mks
 c) Family life today is faced with innumerable problems. List some of them (5mks)
 i) Child abuse and domestic violence
 ii) Diseases and sicknesses
 iii) Unfaithfulness
 iv) Separation and divorce
 v) Childlessness
 vi) Single- parent families
 vii) Jealousy
 viii) Misuse of family resources
 ix) Leadership style Any 5x1=5
 mks
6. a) Give reasons why people work ( 6mks)
 i) For self satisfaction and fulfillment
 ii) For personal development
 iii) To acquire basic essentials of life e.g. food, clothing and shelter
 iv) To give life direction, meaning and dignity
 v) To provide services for the community and fellow human beings and to develop
 and care for the environment
 vi) To acquire wealth and status in society
 vii) To socialize and grow as a member of a community e.g. people participate in
 communal work and projects such as building schools, bridges, churches e.t.c.
 viii) To attain independence. Young people look forward to the time when they will
 not depend on their parents and guardians for the necessity of life Any 6x1=6
 mks
 b) Explain some of the factors that bring about unemployment in Kenya today
 i) The available job opportunities are too limited to absorb the great number of
 school
 leavers and college graduates
 ii) Most young school leavers despise “blue collar” jobs (The manual jobs) and opt
 for “
 White collar jobs”
 iii) Bribery and corruption. This denies job those who are more qualified in
 preference for the unqualified who might have given bribes
 iv) Lack of skills and capital to start self-employment
 v) Bad governance and poor economic policies by the government
 vi) Increase in poverty since 1990’s due to Structural Adjustment Programmes
 (SAPs) imposed by the world bank and IMF on developing countries like Kenya
 vii) International policies of globalisation that have affected the agricultural sector
 which has been the greatest employer in Kenya.
 viii) Retrenchment of workers in the civil service and private sectors
 ix) Increase in crime that has aggravated insecurity in the country. This has
 discouraged local and international investors
 Any 8x1=8 mks
c) What are the negative results brought about by a strike action in a school situation?
 i) May lead to the inciters and culprits being expelled
 ii) It may be very expensive to parents as they pay for damages
 iii) May lead to injuries among students in case of riots
 iv) It leads to loss of study time due to suspension
 v) May lead to poor academic results
 vi) May lead to mistrust between the teachers and students
 vii) Injuries and death may occur when police confronts the strikers
 viii) Loss of employment if teachers are involved
 ix) Victimisation of some individuals especially the ring leader may occur
 Any 6x1=6 mks

SAMPLE PAPER 3
313/2
(a) How prophet Isaiah presented the servant of Yahweh.
 (i) The servant will succeed in his work and will be highly honoured.
 (ii) His success and Honour will surprise many who have witnessed his death.
 (iii) The servant is despised, rejected and ignored by those who are with him.
 (iv) He has nothing attractive, he is very ordinary and simple.
 (v) He is harshly treated, arrested and sentenced to death and killed.
 (vi) He accepts the suffering, which should have been received by other for their sins.
 (vii) His body is buried with the bodies of rich men.
 (viii) He endures all that is done to him in humble silence.
 (ix) Through his sufferings, human beings are reconciled to God.
 (x) It is the will of God that the servants suffer.
 (xi) His death is a sacrifice to bring forgiveness of sins. (8 x 1 = 8mks)
b) How Jesus fulfilled Jeremiah’s teachings on the new covenant.
 i) Jesus inaugurated the new covenant during the Last Supper. He said, "This cup is
 poured out for you in the new covenant in my blood". (LK 22:20)
 ii) The death of Christ on the cross shows that God will not remember their sins anymore.
 iii) Jesus summarized the Mosaic Law into the double commandment of love of God and
 love of one's neighbour LK10: 27. The law of love is eternal.
 (iv) Jesus established the kingdom of God, a new community of God's
 people based on faith and obedience is his teachings.
 (v) Jesus established an everlasting covenant through his death and resurrection.
 (vi) In Jesus, people have direct relationship with God
 (vii) Jeremiah gave hope about restoration which found fulfillment in Jesus who came from
 the Davidic lineage to set up God’s rule on earth.
 (vii) Jesus established the new beginning in the New Testament, which is
